title: Autologous Endothelial Progenitor Cell-Seeding Technology and Biocompatibility Testing For Cardiovascular Devices in Large Animal Model
protocol: Prepare a 60 ml syringe with 15 ml of anticoagulant citrate dextrose solution.
Secure the syringe with a 3-way stop cock for EPC isolation from peripheral pig blood.
Precoat two 12-well plates with Type 1 rat collagen at a concentration of 50 μg/ml, dissolved in 0.02 N acetic acid solution.
Sedate a female Yorkshire pig (45 kg) with Acepromazine at 1.1 mg/kg and Ketamine at 22 mg/kg intramuscularly via a 19 G butterfly needle.
Intubate the pig with an endotracheal tube of 30 cm length and 8 mm inner diameter.
Anesthetize the pig with Isoflurane at 4.5% of tidal volume by mask.
Monitor the pig during the procedure, measuring oxygen saturation, heart rate, and temperature.
Maintain thermoregulation using an automated heated operating table and heating blanket, warming infused fluids as needed.
Place the pig in a supine position on the operating table.
Secure the pig's hind limbs caudolaterally.
Clean the pelvic area with Chlorhexidine followed by DuraPrep sterilization.
Drape the pelvic area.
Insert a 21 G x 7 cm needle into the femoral vein just medial to a palpable femoral pulse.
Cannulate the vein using Seldinger technique.
Connect a prepared 60 ml syringe to the intravascular catheter and draw 45 ml of blood.
Hold pressure on the vessel puncture site for hemostasis (5 min).
Discontinue anesthesia and recover the pig.
Monitor the animal until full recovery before returning it to its cage.
Dilute the drawn blood solution 1:1 with Hank's buffered salt solution.
Layer equal volumes of diluted blood solution and Histopaque to create well-defined layers.
Centrifuge the mixture for 30 min at 740 g with a low break setting.
Collect the mononuclear cell (MNC) layer from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend and wash MNCs three times with Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline (DPBS).
Plate the resuspended MNCs into two 12-well plates in full growth medium at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Slowly change the medium every 24 hours for the first 7 days.
Change the medium every other day after the initial week.
Identify endothelial progenitor cell (EPC) colonies after an average of 7 days.
Expand EPCs in culture once they cover one quarter of the 12-well surface area.
Confirm EPC identity with flow cytometry by testing for presence of CD31 and absence of CD14, CD45.
Section titanium tube longitudinally into three equal 120-degree units (4.5 cm long) using a 72 teeth HHS slitting saw running at 300 RPM.
Keep the cutting area saturated with Tap Magic Cutting Fluid during the cut.
Polish the inner surface of the Ti pieces with a bench grinder and a Scotch-Brite metalworking wheel.
Manually polish the Ti pieces with 3M emery cloth to further smooth and even the surface, removing any visible pits.
Clean the Ti pieces with Alconox soap solution.
Submerge the Ti pieces in aqua regia (1:3 concentrated nitric acid to concentrated hydrochloric acid) for 5 minutes.
Rinse the Ti pieces with several liters of water.
Sonicate the Ti sections in an Alconox soap solution for 16 minutes.
Rinse the Ti sections in deionized water for 30 minutes.
Sonicate the Ti sections again in deionized water for 16 minutes.
Allow the Ti sections to dry in a laminar flow hood.
Cut PVC heat-shrink tubing to a length of 4.5 cm and clean it thoroughly.
Place the three cleaned Ti sections onto a supportive mandrel using tweezers.
Wrap a sleeve of PVC heat-shrink tubing around the Ti sections.
Shrink the tubing with a heat gun while turning the mandrel to wrap the Ti sections tightly together.
Cut silicone tubing to lengths of 2.5 cm and 3.5 cm.
Section a 5 cc plastic syringe at the 0.8 ml mark and keep the 'head piece' with luer end.
Clean 2 x silicone sections by sonication.
Clean syringe 'head piece' by sonication.
Clean luer cap by sonication.
Add silicone tubing to each end of assembled Ti tube, extending by 5 mm over PVC tubing.
Insert cut end of syringe 'head piece' into short silicone tubing so that it abuts Ti tube.
Seal finished Ti tube assembly with one luer cap in Tyvek pouch.
Gas-sterilize sealed assembly with ethylene oxide for 18 hours at 55°C.
Mount synchronous timing motor (10 RPH) onto plexiglass platform.
Connect axle of synchronous timing motor to a syringe holder machined out of aluminum, which fits 5 cc syringe.
Rinse EPCs twice in serum free medium.
Label EPCs with long-term dye PKH26 at a concentration of 4 μM in Diluent C for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Stop labeling reaction by adding porcine serum equal in volume to the dye solution.
Dilute combined solution 1:1 with full growth medium after one minute.
Aspirate liquid and rinse cells three times with full growth medium.
Wash EPCs twice in DPBS without CaCl2, MgCl2.
Cover cells in trypsin and incubate at 37°C for 3 minutes.
Confirm detachment of cells under a light microscope.
Add Trypsin Neutralization Solution in double the volume of trypsin used.
Combine cell solutions into a single tube and mix by pipetting.
Add 10 μl of cell solution into each side of a hemocytometer for counting.
Centrifuge cell solution at 1500 RPH for 5 minutes.
Count cells and resuspend pellet at 2 - 2.5 x 10^6 EPCs/ml in serum free medium.
Lay out sterile towel in biological hood for sterile field.
Open gas-sterilized Ti tube assembly and extra 5 cc syringe onto sterile field.
Remove plunger from 5 cc syringe and keep on field for later use.
Affix luer cap to this syringe.
Pipette the 4.5 - 5 ml EPC suspension into the open syringe barrel.
Insert plunger securely back into open end of syringe.
Hold syringe with cap upward and remove cap.
Insert syringe with luer end first into open silicone tubing of Ti tube assembly until snug; do not advance within Ti tube.
Advance syringe plunger slowly until cell solution reaches top of cut syringe head piece, removing bubbles from system.
Close with luer cap and insert entire assembly into sterile sheath, sealing open end with tape.
Insert this entire assembly into machined syringe holder of 3.7.
Place in incubator at 37°C and adjust platform so that Ti tube portion of seeding chamber is level using water level gauge.
Allow Ti tube assembly to rotate for 30 minutes before implantation.
Premedicate the pig with a Fentanyl patch 24 hours prior to surgery.
Keep the pig NPO overnight before surgery.
Administer Baytril (Enrofloxacin) preoperatively at 5 mg/kg, IM, and continue for 7 days post-surgery every 24 hours as antibiotic prophylaxis.
Sedate the pig according to procedure described under section 1.3.
Intubate the sedated pig.
Anesthetize the pig with a tidal volume of 10-15 ml/kg.
Secure the anesthetized pig in supine position on the operating table.
Measure and monitor oxygen saturation, heart rate, and temperature during the procedure.
Maintain thermoregulation using an automated heated operating table and heating blanket.
Warm the infused fluids to maintain body temperature.
Insert an 18 G IV catheter into the pig's ear vein.
Protect the pig's eyes with Vetropolycin eye drops.
Clean, prep, and drape the pig's abdomen as described in section 1.6.
Incise the midline from the 2nd set of mammary glands cranially to the 2nd to last set caudally using a #15 scalpel blade.
Carry dissection down to the abdominal fascia with electrocautery.
Lift the peritoneum with Mosquito forceps.
Carefully enter the peritoneum with Metzenbaum scissors.
Externalize the urinary bladder.
Place a 3-O Vicryl purse-string suture into the bladder wall.
Make a stab incision in the middle of the bladder wall and insert a 16 F Foley catheter.
Administer intravenous fluids (Lactate Ringers) to titrate urine output to >/= 1 ml/kg/hr during surgery.
Externalize the small and large bowel.
Place two Balfour surgical retractors to expose the posterior aspect of the peritoneal cavity.
Identify the inferior vena cava (IVC).
Free the IVC from surrounding tissue using sharp and blunt dissection.
Skeletonize the vessel from the right renal artery proximal to the bifurcation of the IVC distally.
Ligate all side branches of the IVC segment.
Dissect and ligate the two posterior lumbar veins carefully.
Control a large lumbar vein encountered immediately proximal to the IVC with vessel loops.
Administer 100 USP/kg of heparin immediately prior to clamping the IVC.
Place 45 degree angle surgical clamps distally on the IVC and lumbar vein.
Place 45 degree angle surgical clamps proximally on the IVC and lumbar vein.
Create a longitudinal veinotomy (4 cm) between the proximal and distal clamps using a #11 scalpel blade.
Extend the veinotomy with Potts scissors.
Evacuate any blood from the IVC.
Flush the inner lumen of the IVC with sterile DPBS.
Insert the EPC-seeded Ti tube into the IVC.
Fill the Ti tube with DPBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2.
Close the veinotomy using a 4-0 Prolene running suture.
Remove one proximal clamp to de-air the IVC through back-bleeding.
Place a 'stay-suture' through the vein wall into the PVC tubing.
Close the fascia with O-PDS on a CT needle.
Close the subcutaneous space with 2-O Vicryl in running sutures.
Close the skin with staples.
Administer up to 20 ml of 0.25 % Marcaine subcutaneously along the incision site.
Cover the wound with gauze and Tegaderm.
Give Flunixin subcutaneously as needed for pain.
Give Oxymorphone subcutaneously as needed for pain.
Discontinue anesthesia.
Monitor the pig until it is awake.
Return the pig to its cage.
Monitor the pig twice daily for signs of distress or pain.
Monitor the pig's standing and ambulation.
Monitor stool and urine output in the pig.
Monitor skin color indicating normal perfusion.
Sedate, intubate, and anesthetize the pig after 3 weeks.
Proceed with a laparotomy as previously described.
Dissect out the IVC as previously described.
Explant the Ti tube en-block with the surrounding IVC using heavy scissors.
Euthanize the animal with Euthasol euthanasia solution (390 mg/ml Pentobarbital Sodium and 50 mg/ml Phenytoin Sodium at 1 ml/10 lbs).
Rinse the excised vein segment with Ti tube in DPBS solution.
Photograph its lumen (patent or occluded) with a high resolution digital camera.
Fix the specimen by submersion in 3.7% paraformaldehyde for a minimum of 15 minutes.
Rinse the specimen in DPBS solution.
Very carefully incise the surrounding vein and PVC tubing to open the Ti tube.
Place the sections under a fluorescent microscope with inside surfaces facing the objective/light source.
Image under 550 nm excitation wavelength to visualize PKH26-labeled EPCs in red/orange color.
Draw peripheral blood from a pig.
Isolate EPCs from the drawn blood.
Culture isolated EPCs for expansion.
Line a titanium (Ti) tube device with cultured EPCs.
Implant the Ti tube device into the inferior vena cava of the same pig.
